brief: The linden's shade is a PLACE nobody reads. The tree's shadow is an ellipse drawn once per frame (centre CX + sunX·1.6·shOffset(), CY + 1.2; radii treeR·0.95·shSpread() by treeR·0.8·shSpread()) and no rule consults it — the picnic pair pick a blanket spot at r 9–12 by R() alone, the napper lies at r 2.6 regardless, and the sundial (c124) sits inside it all day at maturity. Step one: count courtyard presence by kind (kid, napper, picnic, sitter, gardener) at 10/13/16 h on HEAD over 10 seeds × 3 summer days and write it into the ledger — at 13:25 on seed 42 the lawn shows none of them (c135). Step two: ONE predicate inLindenShade(x, y) that the draw and the choices both read (one predicate, one definition). Consumers: the picnic pair choose their blanket spot INSIDE the shade when warmth > 0.65 and shadowF() > 0.5 (hot sun), OUTSIDE it when warmth < 0.45 (cool sun), by R() within the chosen set — no new draws in the branch that already draws; the napper's line and personName say 'in the shade of the linden' / 'out in the sun'; sundialName() says 'the sundial, in the linden's shade' when the crown is out and the dial is inside the ellipse. If step one shows the lawn under 2 people at a summer noon on the median seed, say so with the numbers and stop short of retuning capacity — that is the next manager's call, not this brief's.
successLooksLike: probes/shade.mjs, 10 seeds × 3 days at warmth 0.8 vs 0.35: blanket spots inside the ellipse ≥ 80% on hot days, ≤ 20% on cool days, measured at the CHOICE; the sundial's name flips with the crown (bare in winter → no 'shade'); census PASS with only the reshuffle the picnic's spot draw already owns; canvas IDENTICAL to HEAD when inLindenShade is forced false over the run. The ledger carries the courtyard presence histogram.
avoid: Do not move BENCH_SPOTS — all four are 26+ cells from the tree and never in its shade; the shade's consumers are the lawn kinds. Do not thin the tree's shadow to expose the sundial. Do not retune capacity or the spawn shares in this brief.
